rejected.title: Ethical investing
card: An ethical investor chooses where to put money by thinking about values as well as profit. They ask what a company does to people and the environment.
ethical investors may avoid companies that harm people or the environment, such as tobacco makers or coal miners.
ethical investors may choose companies that do good, such as those that make renewable energy or treat their workers fairly.
Different investors hold different values, so what counts as ethical can vary from person to person. Ethical investors may still want a return on their money.
rejected.remember: Ethical investors let values guide which companies they back, as well as the return they hope to earn.

a.q: Which investor is making an ethical investing choice?
opts: Sam buys shares in a solar panel maker to cut pollution
Sam buys shares in a firm because its price rose last year
Sam buys shares in a firm because a friend owns some too
Sam buys shares in a firm because it pays a big dividend
a.why: Sam is choosing a company because it does good for the environment, which is a values-based choice. The other choices rest on price, a friend or payouts, and say nothing about values.
a.clue: Look for the choice based on what the company does to the world.

b.q: Priya wants a good return on her savings. She also does not want her money to support companies that harm the environment. Which choice best fits her aim?
opts: Invest in a company with a record of cutting pollution
Invest in the coal miner with the highest share price
Invest in the company that has the most staff
Invest in the company that is the best known in Australia
b.why: Priya wants a return but also wants to avoid environmental harm, so she picks a company with a good environmental record. A coal miner harms the environment. Size and fame say nothing about whether a company does good or harm.
b.clue: Which company matches her values as well as her wish for a return?

version.title: Ethical investing
card: Ethical investing means choosing where to put money using your values as well as the return you hope to earn. The investor asks what a company does to people and the environment.
many ethical investors leave out companies whose products or actions cause harm, such as tobacco makers or coal miners.
many also pick companies that do good, such as renewable energy firms or businesses known for treating their workers fairly.
People hold different values, so two ethical investors may draw the line in different places. Most still want their money to grow.
version.remember: Ethical investors ask what a company does to the world, not only what it might earn.

a.q: What makes an investment choice an example of ethical investing?
opts: It weighs the company's effect on people and the planet
It picks the company with the highest return last year
It spreads money over many companies to lower the risk
It uses a licensed adviser who acts in your best interests
a.why: Ethical investing brings values into the choice: what the company does to people and the environment. Spreading money to lower risk is a separate idea. It can be done with or without any thought about values.
a.clue: Which choice looks beyond money and risk?

b.q: Leila wants her savings to grow, but she does not want to own part of any business that harms people's health. Which choice fits ethical investing best?
opts: Buy shares in a medical company, not a tobacco company
Buy shares in a tobacco company because profits are high
Buy tobacco shares and give the dividends to charity
Buy shares in whichever company carries the lowest risk
b.why: Leila's value is not harming health, so she avoids tobacco and backs a company that helps people. Giving the dividends away still leaves her money in a tobacco company, which is the harm she wants to avoid.
b.clue: Where does her money actually end up?
